# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# comb dialect
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class CombVariadicRule(SemanticRule):
    """Fold N operands with one binary function, then wrap to the result width."""

    NAME = "comb-variadic"
    #: ``(accumulator, operand) -> int``
    REDUCER: Optional[Callable[[int, int], int]] = None
    #: Result when the operand list is empty.
    IDENTITY = 0

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        reducer = type(self).REDUCER
        if reducer is None:
            raise SemanticError(f"{self.NAME} has no reducer")
        values = self.read_all(op, config)
        if not values:
            return self.IDENTITY
        accumulator = values[0]
        for value in values[1:]:
            accumulator = reducer(accumulator, value)
        return accumulator


class CombAddRule(CombVariadicRule):
    NAME = "comb-add"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.add",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.add(V1, V2) => (V1 +Int V2) modInt 2 ^Int W ...</k>"
    REDUCER = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a + b)


class CombSubRule(CombVariadicRule):
    NAME = "comb-sub"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.sub",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.sub(V1, V2) => (V1 -Int V2) modInt 2 ^Int W ...</k>"
    REDUCER = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a - b)


class CombMulRule(CombVariadicRule):
    NAME = "comb-mul"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.mul",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.mul(V1, V2) => (V1 *Int V2) modInt 2 ^Int W ...</k>"
    REDUCER = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a * b)
    IDENTITY = 1


class CombAndRule(CombVariadicRule):
    NAME = "comb-and"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.and",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.and(V1, V2) => V1 &Int V2 ...</k>"
    REDUCER = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a & b)
    IDENTITY = -1


class CombOrRule(CombVariadicRule):
    NAME = "comb-or"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.or",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.or(V1, V2) => V1 |Int V2 ...</k>"
    REDUCER = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a | b)


class CombXorRule(CombVariadicRule):
    NAME = "comb-xor"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.xor",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.xor(V1, V2) => V1 xorInt V2 ...</k>"
    REDUCER = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a ^ b)


class CombDivURule(SemanticRule):
    """Unsigned division; division by zero saturates, as CIRCT leaves it."""

    NAME = "comb-divu"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.divu",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.divu(V1, V2) => V1 /Int V2 ...</k> requires V2 =/=Int 0"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        lhs, rhs = (self.read_all(op, config) + [0, 0])[:2]
        if rhs == 0:
            width = self.width(op)
            return (1 << width) - 1 if width > 0 else 0
        return lhs // rhs


class CombDivSRule(SemanticRule):
    NAME = "comb-divs"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.divs",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.divs(V1, V2) => signed(V1) /Int signed(V2) ...</k>"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        width = _operand_width(op, 0)
        lhs, rhs = (self.read_all(op, config) + [0, 0])[:2]
        lhs, rhs = _signed(lhs, width), _signed(rhs, width)
        if rhs == 0:
            return (1 << self.width(op)) - 1 if self.width(op) > 0 else 0
        quotient = abs(lhs) // abs(rhs)
        return -quotient if (lhs < 0) != (rhs < 0) else quotient


class CombModURule(SemanticRule):
    NAME = "comb-modu"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.modu",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.modu(V1, V2) => V1 %Int V2 ...</k> requires V2 =/=Int 0"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        lhs, rhs = (self.read_all(op, config) + [0, 0])[:2]
        return 0 if rhs == 0 else lhs % rhs


class CombModSRule(SemanticRule):
    NAME = "comb-mods"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.mods",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.mods(V1, V2) => signed(V1) %Int signed(V2) ...</k>"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        width = _operand_width(op, 0)
        lhs, rhs = (self.read_all(op, config) + [0, 0])[:2]
        lhs, rhs = _signed(lhs, width), _signed(rhs, width)
        if rhs == 0:
            return 0
        remainder = abs(lhs) % abs(rhs)
        return -remainder if lhs < 0 else remainder


class CombShlRule(SemanticRule):
    NAME = "comb-shl"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.shl",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.shl(V, S) => (V <<Int S) modInt 2 ^Int W ...</k>"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        value, amount = (self.read_all(op, config) + [0, 0])[:2]
        width = self.width(op)
        if width and amount >= width:
            return 0
        return value << amount


class CombShrURule(SemanticRule):
    NAME = "comb-shru"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.shru",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.shru(V, S) => V >>Int S ...</k>"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        value, amount = (self.read_all(op, config) + [0, 0])[:2]
        width = self.width(op)
        if width and amount >= width:
            return 0
        return value >> amount


class CombShrSRule(SemanticRule):
    NAME = "comb-shrs"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.shrs",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.shrs(V, S) => signed(V) >>Int S ...</k>"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        width = _operand_width(op, 0)
        value, amount = (self.read_all(op, config) + [0, 0])[:2]
        if width and amount >= width:
            amount = width - 1
        return _signed(value, width) >> amount


class CombMuxRule(SemanticRule):
    """The ALU's selector: ``mux(C, T, F)`` picks ``T`` when ``C`` is set."""

    NAME = "comb-mux"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.mux",)
    K_RULE = (
        "rule <k> comb.mux(1, T, _) => T ...</k>\n"
        "    rule <k> comb.mux(0, _, F) => F ...</k>"
    )

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        values = self.read_all(op, config)
        if len(values) < 3:
            raise SemanticError("'comb.mux' needs a condition and two data operands")
        condition, when_true, when_false = values[0], values[1], values[2]
        return when_true if condition & 1 else when_false


#: ``comb.icmp`` predicates, as explicit two-argument relations.
ICMP_RELATIONS: Dict[str, Callable[[int, int], bool]] = {
    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
    "ult": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "ule": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    "ugt": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "uge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
    "slt": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "sle": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    "sgt": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "sge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}

#: Predicates whose operands are reinterpreted as two's complement first.
SIGNED_PREDICATES = frozenset({"slt", "sle", "sgt", "sge"})


class CombICmpRule(SemanticRule):
    """Comparison: always one bit wide, regardless of the operand width."""

    NAME = "comb-icmp"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.icmp",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.icmp(P, V1, V2) => boolToInt(rel(P, V1, V2)) ...</k>"

    def width(self, op: Operation) -> int:
        return 1

    def predicate(self, op: Operation) -> str:
        attr = op.attributes.get("predicate")
        return str(attr.value) if attr is not None else "eq"

    def side_condition(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> bool:
        return self.predicate(op) in ICMP_RELATIONS

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        predicate = self.predicate(op)
        relation = ICMP_RELATIONS.get(predicate)
        if relation is None:
            raise SemanticError(f"'comb.icmp' has unknown predicate {predicate!r}")
        values = self.read_all(op, config)
        if len(values) < 2:
            raise SemanticError("'comb.icmp' needs two operands")
        lhs, rhs = values[0], values[1]
        if predicate in SIGNED_PREDICATES:
            width = _operand_width(op, 0)
            lhs, rhs = _signed(lhs, width), _signed(rhs, width)
        return 1 if relation(lhs, rhs) else 0


class CombConcatRule(SemanticRule):
    """Operand 0 supplies the most significant bits."""

    NAME = "comb-concat"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.concat",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.concat(V1, V2) => (V1 <<Int W2) |Int V2 ...</k>"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        from circt.hw_dialect import bit_width_of

        values = self.read_all(op, config)
        packed = 0
        for index, value in enumerate(values):
            operands = op.operands
            width = 1
            if index < len(operands) and isinstance(operands[index], Value):
                width = bit_width_of(operands[index].type) or 1
            packed = (packed << width) | (value & ((1 << width) - 1))
        return packed


class CombExtractRule(SemanticRule):
    NAME = "comb-extract"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.extract",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.extract(V, Lo) => (V >>Int Lo) modInt 2 ^Int W ...</k>"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        low = getattr(op, "low_bit", 0)
        attr = op.attributes.get("lowBit")
        if attr is not None:
            low = int(attr.value)
        return self.read(op, config, 0) >> int(low or 0)


class CombReplicateRule(SemanticRule):
    NAME = "comb-replicate"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.replicate",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.replicate(V) => concat(V, ..., V) ...</k>"

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        source_width = _operand_width(op, 0) or 1
        total = self.width(op) or source_width
        count = max(1, total // source_width)
        source = self.read(op, config, 0) & ((1 << source_width) - 1)
        packed = 0
        for _ in range(count):
            packed = (packed << source_width) | source
        return packed


class CombParityRule(SemanticRule):
    """XOR reduction of every bit."""

    NAME = "comb-parity"
    OP_NAMES = ("comb.parity",)
    K_RULE = "rule <k> comb.parity(V) => popCount(V) modInt 2 ...</k>"

    def width(self, op: Operation) -> int:
        return 1

    def compute(self, op: Operation, config: KConfiguration) -> int:
        value = self.read(op, config, 0)
        parity = 0
        while value:
            parity ^= value & 1
            value >>= 1
        return parity


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# seq dialect
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def build_parsed(cls, **kwargs: Any) -> Operation:
        op = super().build_parsed(**kwargs)
        op.operand_widths = []

            op.result(0).type = IntegerType(total)
            op.width = total
        return op

        from circt import CircuitSimulator, find_module
        from k_circt import Kimulator

        for a in self._stimulus():

                self.assertEqual(

                )

        from mlir.printer import print_module
        from circt import CircuitSimulator, find_module
        from k_circt import Kimulator

              %cat = comb.concat %a, %b : i8, i4
              hw.output %cat : i12

        for a in (0, 1, 5, 128, 255):

                expected = (a << 4) | b
                self.assertEqual(expected, sim.evaluate(stimulus)["o"], stimulus)
                self.assertEqual(expected, kim.evaluate(stimulus)["o"], stimulus)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src')
from mlir.parser import parse
from circt import CircuitSimulator, find_module
from k_circt import Kimulator

# Two-phase check: a 3-stage shift register. If a stage saw its predecessor's
# POST-edge value, the input would race through in one cycle.
SHIFT = '''
hw.module @Shift(in %clk: !seq.clock, in %rst: i1, in %d: i8, out q: i8, out q1: i8) {
  %c0 = hw.constant 0 : i8
  %r1 = seq.compreg %d,  %clk reset %rst, %c0 : i8
  %r2 = seq.compreg %r1, %clk reset %rst, %c0 : i8
  %r3 = seq.compreg %r2, %clk reset %rst, %c0 : i8
  hw.output %r3, %r1 : i8, i8
}
'''
sim = CircuitSimulator(find_module(parse(SHIFT), 'Shift'))
kim = Kimulator(parse(SHIFT), 'Shift')
seq = [11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 0, 0, 0]
sv, kv = [], []
for d in seq:
    sim.step({'clk':0,'rst':0,'d':d}); sim.settle()
    kim.step({'clk':0,'rst':0,'d':d}); kim._require_circuit().settle()
    sv.append(sim.output('q')); kv.append(kim.output('q'))
print('sim q :', sv)
print('kim q :', kv)

ref=[]; regs=[0,0,0]
for d in seq:
    regs = [d, regs[0], regs[1]]
    ref.append(regs[2])

}

class TestSequentialAgreement(unittest.TestCase):
    """Two-phase update, clock enable and reset, against a hand-written model."""

    @staticmethod
    def _both(source, name):
        from mlir.parser import parse
        from circt import CircuitSimulator, find_module
        from k_circt import Kimulator

        return (
            CircuitSimulator(find_module(parse(source), name)),
            Kimulator(parse(source), name),
        )

    def test_a_shift_register_delays_by_one_stage_per_cycle(self):
        # If a stage could see its predecessor's post-edge value, the input
        # would race through all three registers within a single cycle.
        source = """
            hw.module @Shift(in %clk: !seq.clock, in %rst: i1, in %d: i8, out q: i8) {
              %c0 = hw.constant 0 : i8
              %r1 = seq.compreg %d,  %clk reset %rst, %c0 : i8
              %r2 = seq.compreg %r1, %clk reset %rst, %c0 : i8
              %r3 = seq.compreg %r2, %clk reset %rst, %c0 : i8
              hw.output %r3 : i8
            }
            """
        sim, kim = self._both(source, "Shift")
        stages = [0, 0, 0]
        for value in (11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 0, 0, 0):
            stimulus = {"clk": 0, "rst": 0, "d": value}
            sim.step(stimulus)
            sim.settle()
            kim.step(stimulus)
            kim.circuit.settle()
            stages = [value, stages[0], stages[1]]
            self.assertEqual(stages[2], kim.output("q"), stimulus)
            self.assertEqual(stages[2], sim.get_output("q"), stimulus)

    def test_clock_enable_holds_the_value(self):
        source = """
            hw.module @Ce(in %clk: !seq.clock, in %en: i1, in %rst: i1,
                          in %d: i8, out q: i8) {
              %c0 = hw.constant 0 : i8
              %r = seq.compreg.ce %d, %clk, %en reset %rst, %c0 : i8
              hw.output %r : i8
            }
            """
        sim, kim = self._both(source, "Ce")
        held = 0
        for enable, value in ((1, 7), (0, 9), (0, 10), (1, 11), (0, 12), (1, 13)):
            stimulus = {"clk": 0, "en": enable, "rst": 0, "d": value}
            sim.step(stimulus)
            sim.settle()
            kim.step(stimulus)
            kim.circuit.settle()
            if enable:
                held = value
            self.assertEqual(held, kim.output("q"), stimulus)
            self.assertEqual(held, sim.get_output("q"), stimulus)

    def test_reset_held_then_released(self):
        with open(os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "counter.mlir")) as handle:
            source = handle.read()
        sim, kim = self._both(source, "Counter")
        expected = 0
        stimulus = [{"clk": 0, "reset": 1}] * 3 + [{"clk": 0, "reset": 0}] * 6
        for step in stimulus:
            sim.step(step)
            sim.settle()
            kim.step(step)
            kim.circuit.settle()
            expected = 0 if step["reset"] else (expected + 1) % 256
            self.assertEqual(expected, kim.output("res"), step)
            self.assertEqual(expected, sim.get_output("res"), step)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

def _parse_paren_type_list(self) -> List[Type]:
        """Parse ``(i4, i8)``, or CIRCT's named result form ``(y: i4, z: i8)``.

        Port names in the result list are recorded in
        :attr:`_last_result_port_names` so the caller can keep them.

        self.expect(TokenKind.LPAREN)
        types: List[Type] = []
        names: List[str] = []
        while not self.check(TokenKind.RPAREN):
            if (

                self.expect(TokenKind.COLON)
            types.append(self._parse_type())
            if not self.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                break
        self.expect(TokenKind.RPAREN)
        self._last_result_port_names = names
        return types

class TestHierarchicalSymbols(unittest.TestCase):
    """``hw.instance`` in CIRCT's own spelling, and what the analyses see."""

    SOURCE = """
        hw.module @Leaf(in %x: i4, out y: i4) {
          %n = comb.add %x, %x : i4
          hw.output %n : i4
        }
        hw.module @Top(in %a: i4, out o: i4) {
          %r = hw.instance "u0" @Leaf(x: %a: i4) -> (y: i4)
          hw.output %r : i4
        }
        """

    def test_instance_parses_into_the_dialect_class(self):
        from mlir.parser import parse

        module = parse(self.SOURCE)
        instance = module.block.operations[1].regions[0].entry_block.operations[0]
        self.assertEqual("hw.instance", instance.name)
        self.assertEqual("u0", instance.instance_name)
        self.assertEqual("Leaf", instance.module_name)
        self.assertEqual(["x"], instance.argument_names)
        self.assertEqual(["y"], instance.get_output_names())
        self.assertEqual(1, instance.num_operands)
        self.assertEqual("i4", str(instance.result(0).type))

    def test_instance_round_trips_in_circt_spelling(self):
        from mlir.parser import parse
        from mlir.printer import print_module

        printed = print_module(parse(self.SOURCE))
        self.assertIn('hw.instance "u0" @Leaf(x: %a: i4) -> (y: i4)', printed)
        self.assertEqual(printed, print_module(parse(printed)))

    def test_instance_verifies_and_its_symbol_reference_binds(self):
        from mlir.ir import Verifier
        from mlir.parser import parse
        from k_circt import resolve_attributes, resolve_symbols, resolve_types

        module = parse(self.SOURCE)
        self.assertEqual([], Verifier.verify(module))

        symbols = resolve_symbols(module)
        self.assertEqual(["Leaf", "Top"], symbols.names())
        self.assertEqual(1, symbols.num_references_resolved)
        self.assertTrue(symbols.is_complete)
        reference = symbols.references[0]
        self.assertEqual("hw.instance", reference.user.name)
        self.assertIs(symbols.operation("Leaf"), reference.target)

        self.assertTrue(resolve_types(module, symbols).is_consistent)
        self.assertTrue(resolve_attributes(module, symbols).is_complete)

    def test_an_instance_of_a_missing_module_is_reported(self):
        from mlir.parser import parse
        from k_circt import resolve_symbols

        module = parse(
            """
            hw.module @Top(in %a: i4, out o: i4) {
              %r = hw.instance "u0" @Absent(x: %a: i4) -> (y: i4)
              hw.output %r : i4
            }
            """
        )
        symbols = resolve_symbols(module)
        self.assertEqual(1, len(symbols.unresolved))
        self.assertFalse(symbols.is_complete)
        self.assertIn("Absent", symbols.errors[0])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)
